stories.title: Islamabad hosts foreign dignitaries for two-day ECO ministerial meeting
summary: Foreign dignitaries arrived in Islamabad on Sunday as Pakistan hosts the two-day 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers, starting today.
Addressing the gathering, DPM Dar also reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to “regional cooperation and advancing shared aspirations for peace, progress and prosperity”.

Monday’s ministerial meeting will be chaired by DPM Dar and attended by foreign ministers and heads of delegations from ECO member states, along with representatives of the organisation’s secretariat and subsidiary bodies.

stories.title: Authorities ban gatherings in five districts of KP for 30 days, citing law and order situation
summary: The notification formalising the restriction, seen by Dawn, said Bajaur Deputy Commissioner (DC) Adnan Farid Afridi approved the restrictions in view of the law and order situation, citing the need for additional measures to safeguard public life and property and maintain peace.

Pillion riding also barred in Lakki Marwat In Lakki Marwat, DC Shahid Rafique imposed a month-long ban on public gatherings, processions, rallies, assemblies and marches within the district’s territorial limits.

According to the order, the restrictions were imposed at the request of the district police officer, who had apprehended that such activities could obstruct public movement, disrupt public services and traffic, and disturb peace and tranquillity.

stories.title: Trump admin warns US air travellers of another messy day
summary: The Trump administration has blamed Friday’s ground stop — meaning no planes can take off — on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines.
That followed about 9,200 flights cancelled and 7,500 delayed on Friday after the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop because of disruptions to air traffic communications.
Duffy called on Friday for $50 billion in funding to upgrade air traffic control systems, up from his earlier request of $30bn after Congress approved $12.5bn last year.

stories.title: In call with Fazl, Bilawal condemns 'govt actions, political vengeance' against JUI-F
summary: SWABI/CHARSADDA: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Sunday spoke to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and condemned the “government’s actions” against him.
The past month has witnessed exchanges of harsh remarks between Fazl and federal ministers, after the JUI-F chief accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights.

JUI-F holds protests across KP JUI-F has decried “baseless and fake propaganda” against Fazl, accused the federal government of resorting to cheap tactics, and questioned actions being taken as part of the anti-encroachment drive in KP.

stories.title: FIA books 8 Pakistanis deported from Turkiye for violating immigration laws
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) said on Sunday it has registered a case against eight Pakistanis deported from Turkiye for allegedly violating immigration laws.
FIA Islamabad registered the case against the eight deportees, who had travelled to Turkiye on work visas but allegedly started working elsewhere illegally instead of joining the companies concerned.
The FIA Islamabad Zone reiterated its resolve to continue action against those involved in human smuggling and violations of immigration laws.

stories.title: Asif hopeful of consensus on new provinces, says it will bring 'progressive' change in political landscape
summary: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Sunday said the country’s political landscape would change in a progressive way if a consensus was reached on the matter of creating new provinces.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah has voiced opposition to the division of Sindh into smaller provinces — although, he said on Wednesday, the PPP had no objection to the creation of new provinces in other parts of the country if their people so desired.

The defence minister recently argued that Pakistan could have as many as 12 provinces if the exercise was guided by administrative requirements rather than linguistic, ethnic or political considerations.

stories.title: HRCP urges end to state crackdowns
summary: In a statement issued at the conclusion of its 40th annual general meeting on Sunday, the HRCP said censorship, surveillance and the alleged misuse of criminal laws were undermining freedom of expression.
It also expressed concern over the 10-year prison sentences handed down to human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Chattha in Oct 2026.

stories.title: GB police register case as PPP protests alleged malpractice in Diamer repolling
summary: PPP’s Attaullah Shah and IPP’s Imam Malik are the main contenders vying for the seat in the partial repolling, held after an election tribunal accepted Malik’s plea and suspended Shah’s assembly membership.

However, after polling concluded, supporters of Shah took to the streets in Diamer district’s Chilas and Gilgit against the alleged removal of ballot boxes from a women’s polling station in Thore Valley.
The tribunal accepted his plea and suspended Shah’s membership and directed the chief election commissioner to conduct re-polling at the three polling stations within 12 days of Nov 6.

stories.title: Theft, old grids, politics fuel debt
summary: Rise of circular debt Circular debt first emerged in the power sector around 2006-07 during the Musharraf regime, when electricity tariffs were frozen despite rising generation costs.
During 2020-22, the government approved the conversion of around Rs804 billion in power-sector circular debt into public debt.

Pakistan's power sector continues to burden consumers with rising electricity tariffs, mounting circular debt and persistent operational inefficiencies, as successive governments struggle to address structural weaknesses in generation and distribution.

stories.title: Pakistan's fiscal dilemma: plug revenue drain first
summary: Energy policy: protecting inefficiency at public expense Pakistan's energy policy represents one of the most expensive structural failures of economic management.

Pakistan's youthful population represents an enormous economic opportunity, yet inadequate education, weak vocational training, insufficient healthcare investment and low female labour-force participation continue to constrain growth.
The real measure of fiscal reform should not be how much additional revenue the government extracts from taxpayers.

stories.title: Battery storage: avoid auto sector mistakes
summary: China dominates the industry, accounting for over 80% of global battery manufacturing capacity and cell production in 2025.
Even major European industrial groups have struggled to compete with China in battery manufacturing.

Pakistan's more realistic starting point would therefore be to assemble battery electric storage systems using competitively priced imported cells and other critical components, while gradually developing domestic technological and manufacturing capabilities.

stories.title: A barcode is only the first link
summary: Since October 9, manufacturers and importers must print a 2D barcode with its own serial number on every pack.
DRAP's guidelines ask distributors, wholesalers and retailers to register, to scan and to report suspect products, but set no date by which they must record what they receive, dispatch or sell.
Manufacturers print the code on the outer box, and many Pakistanis buy their medicine by the strip, so the procedure has to cover loose strips and part packs.

stories.title: Taliban authorities ban cricket content on Kandahar radio
summary: The Taliban authorities have banned radio stations in southern Kandahar from airing content related to cricket, a rapidly growing sport in Afghanistan, two broadcasters and a provincial source told AFP on Sunday.
But the provincial Information and Culture Department told radio stations on Saturday that anything related to cricket is no longer allowed.
Afghanistan’s cricket board did not respond immediately to an AFP request for comment on the decision in Kandahar, which is home to the country’s Taliban leader.

stories.title: Growing crisis
summary: The National Population Council’s executive committee has declared rapid population growth a national emergency.
Provinces must ensure that clinics are adequately equipped, healthcare workers are trained and family planning services reach remote and neglected communities.
Calling population growth a national emergency is easy.

stories.title: Goods exports rise 8.8pc to record $11.4b in first four months of FY27
summary: Pakistan’s goods exports rose 8.8 per cent to a record $11.4 billion in the first four months (July-October) of the current fiscal year, compared with $10.4b in the corresponding period last year, according to official data released on Sunday.

Also Read: High costs squeeze Pakistan's exports Official documents attributed much of the export contraction to the US-Iran conflict, during which shipments fell 32.3 per cent between March and June 2026 compared with the corresponding period a year earlier.
During July-October 2026, Pakistan's exports to Gulf countries registered a 6.4pc decline compared with the corresponding period last year.

stories.title: 'Disgraces spirit of the game': Indian players’ celebrations draw criticism after U-19 Asia Cup final victory over Pakistan
summary: Celebrations by Indian players following their dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the U-19 Asia Cup final on Saturday drew criticism on social media, with several videos appearing to show players making obscene gestures and directing abusive language at their opponents.

Footage circulating online showed some Indian players making inappropriate gestures and shouting at Pakistan players after Mohit Ulva struck the winning boundary off the final delivery at the Al-Amerat Cricket Ground in Muscat.

One video appeared to show players, including Manal Chauhan, making gestures towards Pakistan wicket-keeper-batter Hamza Zahoor, while other clips showed members of the Indian side celebrating aggressively in front of their opponents.

stories.title: Elon Musk, tech leaders sign petition to reinstate Nvidia's Jensen Huang
summary: Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk joined several technology executives in backing an online petition calling for the reinstatement of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang.
"A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too," Musk wrote Friday on the social media platform X.

Huang resigned Thursday as Nvidia's president, CEO and board member amid scrutiny over a reported relationship with a businesswoman suspected by US intelligence officials of ties to Chinese intelligence.

stories.title: Father jailed for one year for failing to pay Rs200,000 in child maintenance
summary: A Rawalpindi family judge, Zeeshan Butt, sentenced a father to one year of rigorous imprisonment for failing to pay Rs200,000 in maintenance for his two young children despite a court order following his divorce from his wife over differences.
During proceedings for implementation of the decree, the court issued six warning notices to the father, directing him to deposit the maintenance amount.
The court observed that its decision constituted a judicial decree and that the father was bound to pay the Rs200,000 maintenance amount.

stories.title: Blasts rattle Bahrain as Iran launches second drone attack in 3 days
summary: Blasts echoed over Bahrain on Sunday as the tiny Gulf nation was rattled by the second Iranian drone attack in three days, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East war.
Iran also fired drones at Bahrain on Friday — the first strikes since September against countries in the energy-rich Gulf, which has been heavily targeted in the eight-month war.
On Friday, following this month’s US strikes on Qeshm island in Hormuz, the Revolutionary Guards said their forces targeted a US early warning radar system in Bahrain.

stories.title: Several arrested during Gen Z demonstration in Berlin
summary: At least 20 people were arrested during a Gen Z protest march in Berlin, police announced on Sunday.
Berlin police reportedly clashed with demonstrators at a "Gen Z regelt" (Gen Z takes charge) march joined by pro-Palestine activists.

1, German police arrested more than 200 people after violent clashes erupted in several cities following largely peaceful Generation Z demonstrations demanding better education funding and social policies.

stories.title: Sandpapergate controversy deepens as ex-Australia bowler Chadd Sayers also claims ‘everyone knew’
summary: Former Australian Test bowler Chadd Sayers backed Usman Khawaja over his “Sandpapergate” claims on Sunday, contradicting Pat Cummins’ denials that he knew nothing about the ball-tampering plot.

Khawaja also alleged sandpaper was used in the second Test at Port Elizabeth, with Sayers saying he was the one who took it from the field. “It (sandpaper) was given to me to take off, so that wasn’t planned or anything.

Warner on Saturday accused the governing body of “a cover-up”, saying that “as far as he knew” they did not interview Hazlewood, Starc or Lyon at the time. “If that’s correct then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn’t know?,” he said.

stories.title: ICC sets tournament calendar until 2035
summary: The ICC Board confirmed the calendar following meetings in Bali, Indonesia, covering the men's Cricket World Cup, T20 World Cup, Champions Trophy and World Test Championship final.

The 2031 Cricket World Cup will be jointly hosted by India and Bangladesh from October 9 to November 23, while the 2035 edition is scheduled for October and November, with the host nation yet to be confirmed.
Australia are the reigning men's Cricket World Cup champions, South Africa hold the World Test Championship title, while India are the current T20 World Cup and Champions Trophy holders.

stories.title: South Korea probes top exam scorer after AI cheating confession
summary: The candidate, who ranked first in both rounds of the qualification exam held in April and July, confessed through his lawyer that he used AI to obtain answers during the tests.
HRDK president Lee Byung-hoon apologised for the incident and said the agency would file a criminal complaint against the test-taker for obstruction of business.
The HRDK said Sunday an “AI inspector” caught a test taker wearing smart glasses during a gas engineer certification exam last month.

stories.title: NASA's Voyager 1 probe poised to achieve mega-distance milestone
summary: Twin spacecraft Voyager 1 and twin spacecraft Voyager 2 were launched 49 years ago, exploring planets in the outer solar system before continuing onward.
"Voyager 1 returned a wealth of new information about Jupiter and Saturn, and their moons," Cummings said.
Voyager 2 is on pace to be ​one light-day away from Earth in nine more years, in November 2035," Cummings said.

stories.title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left the company in August 2025
summary: Megaspeed said on Sunday that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whose ties ​to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have raised US national ‌security concerns, officially left the company on August 30, 2025, and has no current role there.

The Singapore-based cloud-computing company is an Nvidia business partner in ​the Asia-Pacific region and has been in the spotlight after reports ​that Jensen Huang had an affair with former Megaspeed ⁠executive Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of being a ​Chinese spy.
"Megaspeed does not comment on Ms Huang’s personal and private ​matters," the company's statement added.

stories.title: England crush Australia to level ODI series
summary: England ​opener Tom Banton struck a superb century and fast bowler Gus Atkinson claimed four wickets as they beat Australia by 135 runs in the second One-Day International in Adelaide on Sunday to level the three-match series at 1-1.
Australia ‌won the toss and elected to bowl, but Banton set the tone for England's imposing total by taking the attack to the hosts from the outset.
A really rounded side and they showed that tonight." England's attack maintained the pressure throughout, with Atkinson finishing with outstanding figures of 4-28.

stories.title: Netanyahu calls for Israeli unity government, Eisenkot dismisses 'tricks'
summary: Israel’s caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, who in turn dismissed the appeal as a ruse.

Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is “sincere”.
But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his “racist” campaign against Arab parties on Friday.

stories.title: Kids' Choice Awards honour Chris Pratt, BTS
summary: The Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards on Saturday honoured Chris Pratt with the "King of Comedy" title, while ​South Korean boy band BTS took home favorite album for ARIRANG ‌and Spider-Man: Brand New Day won favourite movie.
"I love kids!" Pratt said on ​stage while accepting the award, which celebrates a performer's outstanding ​comedic work across film, television and other entertainment.
The annual fan-voted ceremony honours celebrities ​and franchises across film, television, music and video ​games.

stories.title: Federal Prison Islamabad to be linked with Safe City surveillance system
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Prison Islamabad will also be brought under the surveillance of the Capital Safe City Authority to monitor convicted and undertrial prisoners and alert relevant authorities in real time to prevent any law and order situation inside the jail.

In the event of a law and order situation or any disturbance inside the prison, the Safe City’s surveillance system will alert relevant authorities and departments so they can reach the jail in real time.

Under the first phase, undertrial prisoners will be transferred to the Islamabad prison, followed by convicts involved in white-collar crimes and those arrested by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA).

stories.title: Rs3bn AFIC underpass planned as part of signal-free corridor in Rawalpindi
summary: A senior district administration official told Dawn that the Punjab government wanted to make the road from Koral Chowk to Motorway Chowk signal-free so that commuters could travel from Islamabad Expressway to Motorway Chowk within 20 minutes.

It will soon start work on the underpass on The Mall in front of AFIC, while the Rawalpindi Development Authority will soon begin rehabilitating the Old Airport Road from Koral Chowk to Ammar Chowk,” he said.
Regarding the proposed underpass at Ammar Chowk, he said there was a plan for the project, but it would be taken up after completion of work on the Old Airport Road and AFIC underpass.

stories.title: New emergency department at Islamabad's Pims begins services
summary: ISLAMABAD: The newly launched emergency department at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) has become operational.
More than 69 patients were assessed and treated during its initial hours, while a further 258 patients were seen and managed on Saturday.
The functioning and operational readiness of the operating theatre were also reviewed.

stories.title: Nameer Khan reflects on his unconventional journey from IT to acting
summary: Actor Nameer Khan has reflected on his unconventional journey into the entertainment industry, discussing his transition from information technology to acting, the challenges of establishing himself in showbiz and his approach to learning the craft.
Khan's entry into the entertainment industry was not part of a conventional acting career plan.
Beyond acting, the actor addressed the growing importance of social media in building a career, particularly the need for performers to develop a presence beyond traditional entertainment platforms.

stories.title: Karachi mayor opens exhibition of newspaper adverts at Frere Hall
summary: KARACHI: Mayor Murtaza Wahab on Saturday evening inaugurated an exhibition of newspaper advertisements organised by the All Pakistan Newspapers Society (APNS) at Frere Hall to highlight the significance of such adverts in Pakistan’s history.
If we’re to bring back that kind of creativity, we need to inspire people.
He said the exhibits underline how creatively print advertisements can be used. “Today, creativity is no more, and people have begun copycatting.” Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

stories.title: Top scorer on South Korean tax exam confesses to cheating with AI
summary: It ​has also raised the stakes for organisers of South Korea's high-stakes annual college ​entrance exam this Thursday.
The scandal has rattled a country where standardised tests largely ‌dictate ⁠social mobility and career trajectories, coming just four days ahead of Thursday's annual national college entrance exam.

Prime ⁠Minister Han Seok-sook acknowledged on Friday public concerns over AI-assisted cheating ahead of the national college entrance exam, a high-pressure event that many South Korean students have spent much of their ⁠lives ​preparing for.

stories.title: Peshawar ATC moves to declare Sohail Afridi proclaimed offender in Radio Pakistan attack case
summary: PESHAWAR: An anti-terrorism court here has started proceedings to declare dysfunctional Chief Minister Sohail Afridi as a proclaimed offender in the Radio Pakistan attack case as the relevant police official claimed that Mr Afridi couldn’t be traced.
Last month, the prosecution submitted a supplementary charge-sheet, nominating Mr Afridi and the other four PTI members as accused in the case.

According to a report by investigation officer Deputy Superintendent of Police Khushal Khan, Radio Pakistan Peshawar station director Tufail Ahmad recorded a supplementary statement in light of the forensic findings, nominating the five men as accused.

stories.title: PPP leader calls for Mustafa Kamal’s sacking over ‘anti-Sindh rhetoric’
summary: KARACHI: Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) leader Senator Waqar Mehdi on Saturday demanded the immediate removal of Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal over his statement regarding new provinces.

Raising questions over alleged corruption in Haj and Umrah vaccination arrangements, Senator Mehdi described reports of financial irregularities involving billions of rupees as a serious matter that required a thorough investigation.
The health minister should focus on answering questions about his ministry rather than engaging in divisive political rhetoric,” he added.

stories.title: Lahore's Lakshmi Chowk, surroundings to be restored using British-era techniques
summary: LAHORE: The Punjab government has decided to undertake a comprehensive beautification and restoration project at the historic Lakshmi Chowk and its adjoining areas to revive the architectural character of the locality and preserve its heritage buildings and monuments.
Mr Malik directed the relevant departments to ensure that the original architectural character and structural features of historic buildings were preserved during restoration work.

DC Ijaz, while speaking on the occasion, said that the improvement of the facade on both sides of the road and restoration of historic buildings would be carried out in accordance with high quality construction and finishing standards.

stories.title: Jordan sentences three men to death over deadly church attack
summary: Jordan’s State Security Court sentenced three men to death on Sunday for carrying out an attack on a church in the southern governorate of Karak last month that killed nine people, the state news agency Petra reported.
Read: Jordan king vows crackdown after attack Security forces arrested the three men on October 26 after a shootout at an abandoned house in Karak.
Jordan later acknowledged that its airstrikes had killed civilians in Syria and the two countries agreed to form a joint security committee to review the incident and its consequences.
